msg: crit. 2 at corner R = 49.0 ohm / L = 5.0 nH, best clamped trimmer setting. Measured 35.27 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 49.0 / 7.21 nH (AS-ROUTED residual). Measured 36.84 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 49.0 / 15.0 nH - inside the trimmer's null window, so this one tunes properly. Measured 40.97 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 49.0 / 30.0 nH. Measured 45.20 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 50.0 / 5.0 nH. Measured 36.75 dB - the trimmer is bottomed out and over-correcting, which is why an ideal-null bench would report 78 dB here and this one reports 37.
crit. 2 at the AS-BUILT corner R = 50.0 / 7.21 nH. Measured 39.12 dB - agrees with s11_band.cir rl_r50_p47_fc to 4 decimals, which is the cross-check between the two benches.
crit. 2 at R = 50.0 / 15.0 nH: 59.10 dB. The first nominal-R corner whose exact null the delivered 1-30 pF trimmer can actually reach (needs 1.287 pF).
crit. 2 at R = 51.0 / 5.0 nH. Measured 34.88 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 51.0 / 7.21 nH (select-on-test upper limit, as-routed L). Measured 36.23 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 51.0 / 15.0 nH. Measured 39.20 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 51.0 / 30.0 nH. Measured 36.98 dB.
WORST OF ALL 16 CORNERS: R = 52.5 / 5.0 nH. Measured 30.73 dB = 4.73 dB of margin over crit. 2.
crit. 2 at R = 52.5 / 7.21 nH - the as-routed board with an unselected +5% resistor. Measured 31.19 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 52.5 / 15.0 nH. Measured 31.90 dB.
crit. 2 at R = 52.5 / 30.0 nH. Measured 30.93 dB.

THE RESISTANCE CEILING, quarter 1: at the catalogue +5% resistance no setting of a shunt trimmer gets past ~32.3 dB, because a susceptance cannot correct Re{Zin} (reff_limit.cir proves the mechanism; the X = 0 ceiling is 32.256 dB). 30.73 dB.
same ceiling at 7.21 nH: 31.19 dB.
same ceiling at 15.0 nH: 31.90 dB - the best of the four, because this is the corner nearest a true null.
same ceiling at 30.0 nH: 30.93 dB. The whole R = 52.5 row lives in a 1.16 dB band while L changes by 6x.

WRONG-VALUE CONTRAST, half 1: RL(5.0 nH) - RL(30.0 nH) at R = 52.5 is -0.20 dB. At the binding resistance corner a 6x change in launch inductance is worth a fifth of a decibel - the P2 conclusion 'the resistance tolerance IS the error budget' survives the parasitic correction at this corner.

WRONG-VALUE CONTRAST, half 2 - and this is the bound that encodes review-verify V1. At R = 50.0, RL(5.0 nH) - RL(30.0 nH) = -10.34 dB: with 4.7 pF of FIXED port capacitance the low-inductance corners are over-corrected, so more launch inductance makes the match BETTER, not worse. Re-running this same corner set through the stale 1.3 pF / 1-35 pF model gives +11.43 dB - the opposite sign. A positive reading here means the port parasitic has been reverted.
same inversion at R = 49.0: -9.93 dB.
same sign at R = 51.0 but much smaller (-2.10 dB) - by 51 ohm the resistance error is already competing with the over-correction.

THE HEADLINE CONTRAST: at 15.0 nH, where the trimmer can reach a true null at both resistances, going from R = 50.0 to R = 52.5 costs 27.20 dB of return loss. Compare dl_r525 (0.20 dB for a 6x inductance change). Resistance is still the dominant error term.

the same resistance step at the as-routed 7.21 nH costs 7.93 dB. It is smaller than dr_l15 only because the nominal-R build is itself degraded by the bottomed-out trimmer - 39.12 dB instead of the 71.8 dB a true null would give.
the as-built corner bottoms the trimmer out: 1.000 pF. Cross-checks s11_band.cir ct_r50_p47_pf.
5.0 nH at R = 50 also bottoms out: 1.000 pF (the ideal null needs 2.0 pF TOTAL, i.e. less than C_port alone).
15.0 nH at R = 52.5 still bottoms out (ideal null 5.43 pF total vs 4.7 pF of port): 1.000 pF. The null window shifts up with resistance.

the first corner that does NOT bottom out: 15.0 nH at R = 50 needs 1.287 pF of trimmer on top of the 4.7 pF port. It is 0.29 pF clear of the 1 pF stop, which is why 14.28 nH is quoted as the exact low edge of the null window (tuning_authority.cir lnull_lo_nh).

30.0 nH at R = 50 needs 7.194 pF of trimmer - comfortably inside the delivered 1-30 pF Johanson 5602. Every setting in this 16-corner box is between 1.000 and 7.68 pF, i.e. the whole box lives in the bottom quarter of the part's range.
the largest setting anywhere in the box: 7.680 pF at R = 49.0 / 30.0 nH.
6.097 pF at R = 52.5 / 30.0 nH. Settings fall as resistance rises, because the null susceptance X/(R^2+X^2) does.
